QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_15

answer.text: Assets are sold individually, typically below going-concern value
The company will IPO next year

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes break-up value or liquidation value as the salvage value that would be realised if the business were shut down. It measures the current market value of the company if it were broken up and sold in individual asset pieces, with examples showing scrap and liquidation values typically below going-concern values. The Trap: Liquidation value is not a going-concern, IPO-based, or growth-assumption metric. It deliberately assumes the business stops operating and its assets are sold piecemeal, which usually produces a lower number than DCF or relative valuation methods.
